title: What decimal does each letter stand for on this line?
description: A number line has large marks at 5, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4, with ten small marks between neighbours. Each letter is read as a large mark plus some hundredths. Keeko doubts the first letter and reads nine small marks as nine tenths.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the large mark just before the letter, then add one hundredth for every small mark. Watch for students who read small marks as tenths.

source: A line has large marks at 5, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4, with 10
video_script.why: The child has met hundredths as lengths and now reads a decimal off a line with large and small marks.
video_script.substitution: Read the large mark before the letter, then add one hundredth for each small mark.
video_script.anchor: the number line of the book with large marks from 5 to 5.4 and four letters on it
video_script.wrong_move: Reads nine small marks after five as nine tenths.
video_script.payoff_line: Each letter is a large mark plus its small marks

final_answer.spoken: eigh is five point zero nine, B is five point one three, C is five point two and D is five point three one

maths_rules: ten small marks fill one tenth, so each small mark = 0.1 / 10 = 0.01
C is on the large mark 5.2
video_script.design: One number line from 5 to 5.4 stays on screen. Large marks are tall, small marks are short. Each letter lights up with its own colour while it is read.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number line with large marks from 5 to 5.4, small marks between them and four letters above the line

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the line is drawn
marks.ask: the four letters appear on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a number line.
<bookmark mark='marks'/>The large marks are five, five point one, and so on up to five point four.
Ten small marks sit between neighbouring large marks.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Four letters sit on the line. What decimal does each letter stand for?

beats.on_screen: the number line with its four letters stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the end of the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the gap from 5 to 5.1 is magnified to show 10 small marks; each small mark = 0.01

marks.large: the gap between two large marks is outlined
marks.small: the ten small marks are counted
marks.letter: a letter sits on a small mark

narration: <bookmark mark='large'/>The gap between two large marks is one tenth.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Ten small marks fill that tenth, so each small mark is one hundredth.
<bookmark mark='letter'/>Every letter is a large mark plus some small marks.

beats.on_screen: Given: A is 9 small marks after 5; B is 3 small marks after 5.1; C is on the large mark 5.2; D is 1 small mark after 5.3

marks.given: the position of the letter eigh is written
marks.b: the position of B is written
marks.c: the position of C is written
marks.d: the position of D is written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the letter eigh is nine small marks after five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>B is three small marks after five point one.
<bookmark mark='c'/>C is on the large mark five point two.
<bookmark mark='d'/>D is one small mark after five point three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the decimal at each letter
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to read the decimal at each letter.

marks.a1: the letter eigh lights up and the large mark 5 is written
marks.a2: nine hundredths are added to the 5

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Step one, read the letter eigh as the large mark five plus nine small marks.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Nine small marks are nine hundredths.
Five plus zero point zero nine gives five point zero nine.

marks.b1: B lights up and the large mark 5.1 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='b1'/>Step two, read B as the large mark five point one plus three small marks.
<bookmark mark='b2'/>Five point one plus zero point zero three gives five point one three.

beats.on_screen: C is on the large mark 5.2, no small marks

marks.c1: C lights up on the large mark

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, C sits exactly on a large mark.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>It has no small marks to add, so it reads five point two.

marks.d1: D lights up and the large mark 5.3 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step four, read D as the large mark five point three plus one small mark.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Five point three plus zero point zero one gives five point three one.

marks.vals: the four readings sit beside their letters

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each letter is a large mark plus its small marks.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>Eigh reads five point zero nine, and B reads five point one three.
C reads five point two, and D reads five point three one.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: eigh = 5.9; the bubble is crossed out and 5.9 is shown as a large mark near 6

marks.fix: 5.9 jumps to its large mark near six
marks.tenths: nine small marks shrink into a short stretch after five

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the letter eigh is five point nine, since it has nine small marks.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But five point nine is a large mark, close to six.
<bookmark mark='tenths'/>Nine small marks after five are nine hundredths, not nine tenths.
